question:
Who among the following was the second ruler of the Maurya Empire?

[SSC GD 2024]
options: Bindusara
Brihadratha
Ashoka
Chandragupta Maurya
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bindusara

Explanation:
Bindusara was the second ruler of the Maurya Empire. He was the son of Chandragupta Maurya and the father of Ashoka. He ruled from approximately 298 BCE to 273 BCE. Bindusara was also known as 'Amitraghata' (Slayer of Enemies). During his reign, the Mauryan Empire expanded further into South India. He maintained friendly relations with the Greek ruler Seleucus and promoted trade.

Extra Facts:
Bindusara managed a vast empire with 16 provinces during his rule. He showed tolerance towards Jainism and Buddhism. The Greek ambassador Deimachus resided in his court. After his death, Ashoka gained the throne after a power struggle.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन, मौर्य साम्राज्य का दूसरा शासक था ?

[SSC GD 2024]
options_hi: बिंदुसार
बृहद्रथ
अशोक
चन्द्रगुप्त मौर्य
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है बिंदुसार

Explanation:
बिंदुसार मौर्य साम्राज्य का दूसरा शासक था। वह चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य का पुत्र और अशोक का पिता था। उसने लगभग 298 ईसा पूर्व से 273 ईसा पूर्व तक शासन किया। बिंदुसार को 'अमित्रघात' (दुश्मनों का विनाशक) भी कहा जाता था। उसके शासनकाल में मौर्य साम्राज्य का विस्तार दक्षिण भारत तक हुआ। उसने यूनानी शासक सेल्यूकस के साथ मैत्रीपूर्ण संबंध बनाए रखे और व्यापार को बढ़ावा दिया।

Extra Facts:
बिंदुसार ने अपने शासनकाल में 16 प्रांतों वाले विशाल साम्राज्य को संभाला। उसने जैन और बौद्ध धर्म के प्रति सहिष्णुता दिखाई। उसके दरबार में यूनानी राजदूत डायमेकस भी रहा था। उसकी मृत्यु के बाद अशोक ने सत्ता संघर्ष के बाद सिंहासन प्राप्त किया।

question:
Who among the following Mauryan kings turned to Buddhism and its tenet of non-violence after the Kalinga war ?

[SSC CPO 2023]
options: Ashoka
Dasharatha
Chandragupta Maurya
Bindusara
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ashoka

Explanation:
Emperor Ashoka embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga War (261 BCE). The war was so brutal that it deeply affected Ashoka's conscience. Disturbed by the massive bloodshed and destruction, he adopted the principles of non-violence (Ahimsa) and Dhamma. He propagated Buddhism and played a crucial role in spreading it across Asia. Ashoka conveyed his messages to the public through edicts and pillars, which are significant historical sources today.

Extra Facts:
The Kalinga War was the last major expansion war of the Mauryan Empire. After this, Ashoka adopted the policy of 'Dhamma Vijaya' (victory through righteousness), prioritizing peace and morality over war. He organized the Buddhist Council and provided state patronage to Buddhism.

question_hi:

Explanation:
सम्राट अशोक ने कलिंग युद्ध (261 ईसा पूर्व) के बाद बौद्ध धर्म अपनाया था। यह युद्ध इतना भीषण था कि इसने अशोक के मन को झकझोर दिया। युद्ध में हुए नरसंहार और विनाश से व्यथित होकर उन्होंने अहिंसा और धम्म के सिद्धांतों को अपनाया। उन्होंने बौद्ध धर्म का प्रचार किया और पूरे एशिया में इसे फैलाने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई। अशोक ने शिलालेखों और स्तंभों के माध्यम से अपने संदेशों को जनता तक पहुँचाया।

Extra Facts:
कलिंग युद्ध मौर्य साम्राज्य के विस्तार का अंतिम बड़ा युद्ध था। इसके बाद अशोक ने 'धम्म विजय' की नीति अपनाई, जिसमें युद्ध के बजाय शांति और नैतिकता को प्राथमिकता दी गई। उन्होंने बौद्ध संगीति का आयोजन करवाया और बौद्ध धर्म को राजकीय संरक्षण दिया।

question:
Magasthenes was an ambassador who was sent to the court of Chandragupta Maurya by the _______ruler named Seleucus Nicator.

[NTPC CBT 2]

Arab

Greek

Persian
solution:

Explanation:
Seleucus Nicator was a Greek ruler and one of the successors of Alexander the Great. He sent Megasthenes as an ambassador to the court of Chandragupta Maurya. Megasthenes wrote a detailed account of the Mauryan Empire in his book 'Indica'. This historical event took place around 305 BCE when Seleucus made a treaty with Chandragupta and had to cede some territories. It was after this treaty that Megasthenes was sent to India.

question:
Who wrote the Mauryan period book Arthashastra?

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: Bindusara
Vishnu Gupta
Chandragupta Maurya
Bhanugupta
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Vishnu Gupta

Explanation:
The Arthashastra is a significant Mauryan-era treatise written by Vishnu Gupta (Kautilya or Chanakya). This text covers politics, economics, governance, and military strategy. Chanakya was the mentor and chief advisor of Chandragupta Maurya, playing a crucial role in establishing the Mauryan Empire. The Arthashastra consists of 15 books and 180 chapters, providing detailed insights into statecraft.

Extra Facts:
The Arthashastra is considered the first systematic work on state administration in ancient India. It discusses taxation, judicial systems, espionage, and warfare. Chanakya introduced the concept of an ideal state through the 'Saptanga Theory', which outlines seven essential elements of a kingdom.

question_hi:
मौर्यकालीन पुस्तक अर्थशास्त्र की रचना किसने की थी?

[SSC CGL 2023]
options_hi: बिन्दुसार
विष्णु गुप्त
चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य
भानुगुप्त
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है विष्णु गुप्त

Explanation:
अर्थशास्त्र मौर्यकालीन एक महत्वपूर्ण ग्रंथ है, जिसकी रचना विष्णु गुप्त (कौटिल्य या चाणक्य) ने की थी। यह ग्रंथ राजनीति, अर्थव्यवस्था, शासन प्रणाली और सैन्य रणनीति पर आधारित है। चाणक्य, चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य के गुरु और मुख्य सलाहकार थे, जिन्होंने मौर्य साम्राज्य की स्थापना में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई। अर्थशास्त्र में 15 अधिकरण और 180 प्रकरण हैं, जो राज्य के संचालन के विभिन्न पहलुओं पर विस्तृत जानकारी प्रदान करते हैं।

Extra Facts:
अर्थशास्त्र को प्राचीन भारत का सबसे पहला व्यवस्थित ग्रंथ माना जाता है जो राज्य प्रशासन से संबंधित है। इसमें कर व्यवस्था, न्याय प्रणाली, जासूसी तंत्र और युद्धनीति जैसे विषयों का विस्तृत वर्णन है। चाणक्य ने इस ग्रंथ के माध्यम से एक आदर्श राज्य की अवधारणा प्रस्तुत की, जिसे 'सप्तांग सिद्धांत' कहा जाता है।

question:
Who among the following Greek rulers sent Megasthenes to the court of Chandragupta Maurya?

[SSC GD 2022]
options:
Amyntas III

Amyntas II

seleucus nicator

Philip II
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Seleucus Nicator

Explanation:
Seleucus Nicator sent Megasthenes to the court of Chandragupta Maurya. This event occurred around 305 BCE when Seleucus made a treaty with Chandragupta Maurya. As part of the treaty, Seleucus married his daughter to Chandragupta and received 500 war elephants in return. Megasthenes, a Greek ambassador and historian, wrote detailed accounts of the Mauryan Empire in his book 'Indica', which is a crucial source for understanding ancient Indian history.

Extra Facts:
Megasthenes described the grandeur of Pataliputra (modern Patna), Mauryan administration, and society in his book 'Indica'. He referred to Chandragupta Maurya as 'Sandrocottus'. Seleucus Nicator was one of Alexander's generals and founded the Seleucid Empire. Chandragupta Maurya defeated Seleucus and gained control over parts of western India.

question:
Who was the teacher of Chandergupta Maurya?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Vishnu Sharma
Vishnu Gupta
Skandagupta
Kalhan
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Vishnu Gupta (Chanakya)

Explanation:
Chandragupta Maurya's teacher was Vishnu Gupta, also known as Chanakya or Kautilya. Chanakya was a renowned political strategist, economist, and teacher at Takshashila University. He played a crucial role in helping Chandragupta overthrow the Nanda dynasty and establish the Mauryan Empire. Chanakya authored the Arthashastra, a seminal text on ancient Indian statecraft and economics.

Extra Facts:
Chanakya used his strategic acumen to expand the Mauryan Empire through policies like Sama, Daam, Dand, Bhed (conciliation, gifts, punishment, and division). Chandragupta Maurya, under Chanakya's guidance, defeated Seleucus Nicator and secured territories in western India.

question:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 1857
1876
1837

solution:

Explanation:
James Prinsep, a British archaeologist and philologist, deciphered the Brahmi script in 1837 and interpreted Ashoka's edicts. This was a major historical breakthrough as it revealed crucial information about the Mauryan Empire and Emperor Ashoka. Prinsep studied inscriptions found at Sanchi Stupa and other sites to decode Brahmi, revolutionizing the understanding of Indian history.

Extra Facts:
The Brahmi script is one of the oldest scripts in India, from which modern scripts like Devanagari, Tamil, and Telugu evolved. Ashoka's edicts, engraved on rocks and pillars, mainly discuss Buddhism, morality, and governance principles. Prinsep's discovery gave a new direction to Indian archaeology.

solution:

Extra Facts:
Shravanabelagola is a major Jain pilgrimage site, famous for the colossal statue of Gommateshwara (Bahubali). Chandragupta's reign saw the expansion of the Mauryan Empire, including his victory over Seleucus Nicator, which secured western India.

question:
The Hathigumpha Inscription was inscribed in which of the following historical regions of India?

[SSC MTS 2024]

solution:

Explanation:
The Hathigumpha Inscription is a significant historical record of India, located in the Udayagiri Hills of Kalinga (present-day Odisha). It was inscribed by Kharavela, the great king of the Chedi dynasty of Kalinga. The inscription is written in the Brahmi script and Prakrit language. It details Kharavela's military campaigns, religious activities, and social achievements. Dating back to the 2nd century BCE, this inscription is a crucial source for understanding the history of Kalinga.

Extra Facts:
Kharavela established Kalinga as a powerful empire. He invaded Magadha and conquered Pataliputra. The Hathigumpha Inscription mentions Jainism, as Kharavela was a follower of Jainism. It also provides insights into Kalinga's economic prosperity and cultural development.

[NTPC CBT 2]

Chandragupta Maurya

solution:

Explanation:
Emperor Ashoka (272/268-231 BCE) had his inscriptions engraved on rocks and pillars during his reign. These inscriptions were written in Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts and contained the principles of his Dhamma (Dharma). Extra Facts:
Ashoka's Kalinga War (261 BCE) was a turning point in his life, after which he renounced violence and embraced Buddhism. He constructed stupas and viharas and sent his son Mahendra and daughter Sanghamitra to Sri Lanka to spread Buddhism.

Emperor Ashoka sent his son Mahendra and daughter Sanghamitra to Ceylon (Sri Lanka) to spread the principles of Dhamma (Buddhist ethics and compassion). This mission was sent in the 3rd century BCE and played a crucial role in establishing Buddhism in Sri Lanka. King Devanampiya Tissa of Ceylon embraced Buddhism and made it the state religion. This mission laid the foundation of Buddhism in Sri Lanka, which remains a dominant religion there today.

Extra Facts:
Ashoka undertook several Dhamma missions during his reign to propagate Buddhism abroad. Sanghamitra carried a branch of the Bodhi tree from Bodh Gaya and planted it in Sri Lanka, which still exists in Anuradhapura. This mission symbolizes the cultural ties between the Mauryan Empire and Sri Lanka.

लंका
कंबोडिया

सम्राट अशोक ने अपने बेटे महेंद्र और बेटी संघमित्रा को लंका (श्रीलंका) में बौद्ध धर्म के सिद्धांतों को फैलाने के लिए भेजा था। यह मिशन तीसरी शताब्दी ईसा पूर्व में भेजा गया था और इसका उद्देश्य धम्म (बौद्ध नैतिकता और करुणा) का प्रचार करना था। लंका के राजा देवानाम्पिय तिस्स ने बौद्ध धर्म को अपनाया और इसे राजधर्म बना दिया। इस मिशन ने श्रीलंका में बौद्ध धर्म की नींव रखी, जो आज भी वहाँ का प्रमुख धर्म है।

question:
Which of the following Mauryan inscriptions is NOT located in present-day India ?

[SSC GD 2024]
options: Kalsi
Kandahar
Maski
Girnar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kandahar

Explanation:
The Mauryan inscriptions were propagated by Emperor Ashoka and were spread across the empire. The Kandahar inscription is located in present-day Afghanistan, which was part of the Mauryan Empire at that time but is not part of India today. The other options—Kalsi (Uttarakhand), Maski (Karnataka), and Girnar (Gujarat)—are all located in India. Ashoka's edicts were written in Brahmi, Kharosthi, Greek, and Aramaic scripts, reflecting the diversity of his empire.

Extra Facts:
Mauryan inscriptions can be broadly categorized into two types: Rock Edicts (engraved on rocks) and Pillar Edicts (engraved on pillars). Ashoka's edicts contain teachings of Dhamma (Dharma), social morality, and administrative instructions. These inscriptions are among the oldest written records in Indian history.

solution_hi:

Explanation:
मौर्यकालीन शिलालेख सम्राट अशोक द्वारा प्रचारित किए गए थे और ये पूरे साम्राज्य में फैले हुए थे। कंधार का शिलालेख वर्तमान में अफगानिस्तान में स्थित है, जो उस समय मौर्य साम्राज्य का हिस्सा था, लेकिन आज भारत का हिस्सा नहीं है। अन्य विकल्प कलसी (उत्तराखंड), मास्की (कर्नाटक), और गिरनार (गुजरात) भारत में ही स्थित हैं। अशोक के शिलालेखों को ब्राह्मी, खरोष्ठी, ग्रीक और अरामाइक लिपियों में लिखा गया था, जो उनके साम्राज्य की विविधता को दर्शाते हैं।

question:
Which of the following was NOT one of the basic attributes of Ashokas' Dhamma?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Political unification
Ahimsa
Celibacy
Secularism
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Celibacy

Explanation:
Emperor Ashoka's Dhamma was based on principles like non-violence (Ahimsa), tolerance, social harmony, moral conduct, and religious coexistence. Through his edicts, Ashoka promoted political unification and supported secularism by respecting all religions. However, celibacy was not a part of Ashoka’s Dhamma, as it was more associated with certain Buddhist sects, whereas Ashoka’s Dhamma focused on universal ethical principles applicable to all sections of society.

Extra Facts:
Ashoka appointed officers called Dhamma Mahamatras to propagate moral teachings. He banned animal slaughter and promoted medical facilities. His inscriptions refer to him as Piyadasi (Beloved of the Gods) and Devanampiya (Beloved of the Gods), reflecting his religious policies.

question:
What was the customs and toll collector known as in the Maurya administration?

[CONSTABLE EXECUTIVE ]
options: Shulkaadhyaksha
Akshapataladhyaksha
Navadhyaksha
Amatyas
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Shulkaadhyaksha

Explanation:
In the Mauryan administration, the 'Shulkaadhyaksha' was the official responsible for collecting customs and toll taxes. This position was a crucial part of the Mauryan economic system. Kautilya's 'Arthashastra' mentions this role, where the Shulkaadhyaksha was tasked with collecting taxes on trade routes, borders, and markets. These taxes were a major source of revenue, ensuring the empire's financial stability.

Extra Facts:
The Mauryan Empire had a well-organized taxation system, including agricultural tax (Bhaga), trade tax (Shulka), and industrial taxes. The Arthashastra elaborately describes taxation principles. Other key officials in the Mauryan administration included the 'Samaharta' (chief revenue collector) and 'Sannidhata' (treasurer), who managed finances at central and provincial levels.

मौर्य प्रशासन में 'शुल्काध्यक्षा' सीमा शुल्क और टोल एकत्र करने वाले अधिकारी को कहा जाता था। यह पद मौर्य साम्राज्य की आर्थिक व्यवस्था का एक महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा था। कौटिल्य के 'अर्थशास्त्र' में इसका उल्लेख मिलता है, जहाँ शुल्काध्यक्षा को व्यापारिक मार्गों, सीमाओं और बाजारों पर लगने वाले करों के संग्रह का जिम्मेदार बताया गया है। यह राजस्व का एक प्रमुख स्रोत था और इससे साम्राज्य की आर्थिक स्थिरता बनी रहती थी।

question:
Deimachus who was a Greek ambassador came to India during the reign of the Mauryan king, ____ .

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: Shatadhanvan
Bindusara
Ashoka
Chandragupta Maurya
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bindusara

Explanation:
Deimachus was a Greek ambassador sent by Antiochus I, the son of Seleucus Nicator, to the court of the Mauryan emperor Bindusara. Bindusara was the son of Chandragupta Maurya and the father of Ashoka, ruling approximately from 297-273 BCE. The arrival of Greek ambassadors indicates diplomatic relations between the Mauryan and Greek empires. Apart from Deimachus, Megasthenes (sent to Chandragupta’s court) and Dionysius (sent to Ashoka’s court) also visited India.

Extra Facts:
Bindusara was also known as 'Amitraghata' (Slayer of Enemies). During his reign, the Mauryan Empire extended to South India. He patronized scholars of the Ajivika sect. A rebellion in Taxila during his rule was suppressed by Ashoka.

question:
During the Mauryan period, Kalinga was the ancient name of which dominant present- day coastal state?

[CONSTABLE EXE 2023]
options: Andhra Pradesh
Tamil Nadu
Odisha
Karnataka
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Odisha

Explanation:
During the Mauryan period, Kalinga was the ancient name of present-day Odisha and parts of northern Andhra Pradesh. This region was known for its rich culture and naval power. In 261 BCE, the Mauryan emperor Ashoka invaded Kalinga, leading to a brutal war. The massive bloodshed in this battle deeply affected Ashoka, prompting him to renounce war and embrace Buddhism. The Kalinga War is mentioned in Ashoka's edicts, where he emphasized the propagation of Dhamma (righteousness) after the war.

Extra Facts:
Kalinga's history is not limited to the Mauryan era. It was ruled by famous kings like Kharavela of the Mahameghavahana dynasty. The capital of Kalinga was Tosali (modern-day Dhauli near Bhubaneswar). The region was a significant trade hub, with maritime links to Southeast Asia.

ओडिशा

Explanation:
मौर्य काल के दौरान, कलिंग वर्तमान ओडिशा और आंशिक रूप से आंध्र प्रदेश के उत्तरी भाग का प्राचीन नाम था। यह क्षेत्र अपनी समृद्ध संस्कृति और नौसैनिक शक्ति के लिए प्रसिद्ध था। 261 ईसा पूर्व में मौर्य सम्राट अशोक ने कलिंग पर आक्रमण किया, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप भीषण युद्ध हुआ। इस युद्ध में हुए भारी रक्तपात ने अशोक को युद्ध से विरक्त कर दिया और उन्होंने बौद्ध धर्म अपना लिया। कलिंग युद्ध का उल्लेख अशोक के शिलालेखों में मिलता है, जिसमें उन्होंने इस युद्ध के बाद धम्म (धर्म) के प्रचार पर जोर दिया।

three

Explanation:
According to Asokan inscriptions, there were five major political centres in the Mauryan Empire. These centres were Pataliputra (capital), Taxila, Ujjain, Tosali, and Suvarnagiri. These are mentioned in Asoka's major rock and pillar edicts. These centres were crucial for administrative, military, and economic activities. Asoka effectively governed his empire through these centres, and they played a significant role in the spread of Buddhism.

Extra Facts:
The Mauryan Empire was the first major empire in India, founded by Chandragupta Maurya. Asoka embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga War and used inscriptions to propagate 'Dhamma'. These inscriptions were written in Brahmi, Kharosthi, Aramaic, and Greek scripts.

Ashokan Minor Rock Edicts are found in different parts of India. Which of the following is NOT a find spot of Ashokan Minor Rock Edicts in Karnataka?

Rupnath

Explanation:

These edicts are found in various parts of India, including Karnataka. Brahmagiri, Gavimath, and Maski are major sites of Ashoka's Minor Rock Edicts in Karnataka. However, Rupnath is located in the Satna district of Madhya Pradesh, not in Karnataka. The edict found here explicitly mentions Ashoka's name, giving it special significance.

Extra Facts:
Ashoka's edicts can be divided into two categories - Minor Rock Edicts and Major Rock Edicts. These are written in the Brahmi script and in the Prakrit language. The Maski (Karnataka) edict was the first to mention Ashoka's name, whereas earlier he was referred to as 'Devanampiya Piyadassi' (Beloved of the Gods).

Who was the grandfather of King Ashoka ?

options: Vitashoka

Extra Facts:
Chandragupta Maurya defeated Seleucus Nicator and gained control over parts of western India. He later embraced Jainism and spent his last days in asceticism at Shravanabelagola. His reign is noted for its strong administrative and military systems, as described in the Arthashastra.

question:
Megasthenes wrote about Pataliputra, saying that it is a large and beautiful city that is surrounded by a massive wall. It has 570 towers and ____ gates.

Explanation:
Megasthenes, a Greek ambassador and historian, provided a detailed account of Pataliputra during his stay in the court of Chandragupta Maurya. In his book 'Indica', he described Pataliputra as a large and beautiful city enclosed by a massive wall. The wall had 570 towers and 64 gates. This description highlights the grandeur of the Mauryan Empire and its advanced urban planning. According to Megasthenes, Pataliputra had a robust security system and was a major hub for trade and administration.

Extra Facts:
Megasthenes' 'Indica' is a crucial source for ancient Indian history, though the original text is lost. References to it are found in other works. Pataliputra (modern-day Patna) was the capital of the Mauryan Empire, located on the banks of the Ganges River. Under Chandragupta Maurya's rule, it was one of the largest and most prosperous cities in the world.

question:
One of the earliest explorers who visited India was Megasthenes. Which country did he hail from?

[RRB ALP CBT]
options: Greece
Spain
Egypt
Italy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Greece

Explanation:
Megasthenes was a Greek ambassador, historian, and explorer who visited India in the 4th century BCE. He was sent as an envoy by Seleucus Nicator (one of Alexander’s generals) to the court of Chandragupta Maurya. Megasthenes documented his observations in the book 'Indica', which provides valuable insights into ancient Indian society, economy, and administration. His work remains a crucial source for studying early Indian history.

Extra Facts:
Megasthenes traveled to Pataliputra (modern-day Patna), the capital of the Mauryan Empire. He described India’s caste system, agricultural practices, and military organization. Although some of his accounts were exaggerated or inaccurate, his writings offer a significant foreign perspective on ancient India.

question:
Since the Maurya Empire was so large, different parts were ruled separately. The emperor had direct control over the areas around ___________.

[SSC GD 2022]
options: Pataliputra
Taxila
Ujjain
Lumbini
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Pataliputra

Explanation:
The Maurya Empire (322-185 BCE) was a vast empire in ancient India, with its capital at Pataliputra (modern-day Patna). Due to the empire's enormous size, distant provinces were governed through regional administrators or local rulers. However, the emperor had direct control over the capital Pataliputra and its surrounding areas. This region was the administrative, military, and economic hub of the empire. Emperors like Chandragupta Maurya, Bindusara, and Ashoka ruled the empire from here.

Extra Facts:
Pataliputra was located on the banks of the Ganges River and was a major center of trade and culture. Megasthenes, the Greek ambassador in Chandragupta’s court, described the grandeur of Pataliputra in his book 'Indica'. During Ashoka's reign, the city further flourished and became a major center of Buddhism.

question:
The earliest deciphered epigraphy of Ashoka‘s inscription in India was written in which script?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Harappan
Kharosthi
Devanagari
Brahmi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Brahmi

Explanation:
The earliest deciphered inscriptions of Emperor Ashoka in India were written in the Brahmi script. These inscriptions were first deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837 CE. Ashoka's edicts were primarily engraved on rocks and pillars, containing principles of Buddhism, administrative policies, and human values. The Brahmi script is considered the mother script of most modern Indian scripts.

Extra Facts:
Ashoka's inscriptions are of three types: Rock Edicts (on boulders), Pillar Edicts (on pillars), and Cave Inscriptions (in caves). These inscriptions were written in Prakrit rather than Sanskrit. Ashoka used local languages and scripts to communicate his messages to the common people.

Who was the founder of the Mauryan dynasty?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Vikramaditya

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chandragupta Maurya

Explanation:
Chandragupta Maurya was the founder of the Mauryan dynasty, who established the Mauryan Empire in 322 BCE after defeating the Nanda dynasty. He was guided by his mentor and prime minister, Chanakya (Kautilya). Chandragupta built a vast empire covering most of northern India and even defeated Seleucus Nicator to annex parts of western India. In his later years, he embraced Jainism and retired to Shravanabelagola.

Extra Facts:
The Mauryan Empire was India's first unified and powerful empire. Chandragupta's grandson, Ashoka, adopted Buddhism after the Kalinga War and promoted it widely. The Mauryan period saw the composition of texts like Arthashastra (by Kautilya), a crucial source on politics and economics.

question:
The capital of the Maurya Empire was _____.

[SSC GD 2024]
options: Ujjaini
Suvarnagiri
Pataliputra
Takshila
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Pataliputra

Explanation:
The capital of the Maurya Empire (322-185 BCE) was Pataliputra, located in present-day Patna, Bihar. This city was situated at the confluence of the Ganges and Son rivers, making it strategically and economically significant. Chandragupta Maurya founded the empire, and the Greek ambassador Megasthenes described Pataliputra in detail in his book 'Indica'. The city flourished as an administrative, cultural, and trade hub. During Ashoka's reign, it also became a major center of Buddhism.

Extra Facts:
Pataliputra was also known as 'Kusumapura'. During the Mauryan period, it had a massive fort surrounded by wooden walls, as mentioned by Megasthenes. Later, the Gupta Empire (3rd-6th century CE) also made it their capital. The city was close to the renowned Nalanda University, a prominent ancient educational center.

question_hi:
मौर्य साम्राज्य की राजधानी ________ थी।

[SSC GD 2024]
options_hi: उज्जयिनी
सुवर्णगिरि
पाटलिपुत्र
तक्षशिला
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है पाटलिपुत्र

Explanation:
मौर्य साम्राज्य (322-185 ईसा पूर्व) की राजधानी पाटलिपुत्र थी, जो वर्तमान में पटना, बिहार में स्थित है। यह नगर गंगा और सोन नदियों के संगम पर बसा था, जिसने इसे रणनीतिक और आर्थिक रूप से महत्वपूर्ण बनाया। चंद्रगुप्त मौर्य ने इस साम्राज्य की स्थापना की और मेगस्थनीज (यूनानी राजदूत) ने अपनी पुस्तक 'इंडिका' में पाटलिपुत्र का विस्तृत वर्णन किया है। यह नगर प्रशासनिक, सांस्कृतिक और व्यापारिक केंद्र के रूप में विकसित हुआ। अशोक के शासनकाल में यह बौद्ध धर्म का प्रमुख केंद्र भी बना।

Extra Facts:
पाटलिपुत्र को 'कुसुमपुर' के नाम से भी जाना जाता था। मौर्य काल में यहाँ लकड़ी की दीवारों से घिरा एक विशाल किला था, जिसका उल्लेख मेगस्थनीज ने किया है। बाद में, गुप्त साम्राज्य (3री-6ठी शताब्दी ईस्वी) ने भी इसे अपनी राजधानी बनाया। यह नगर महान नालंदा विश्वविद्यालय के निकट स्थित था, जो प्राचीन भारत का प्रमुख शिक्षा केंद्र था।
